    40	\section{Key theorem forms}
    41	
    42	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    43	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    44	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    45	correlation estimate
    46	\[
    47	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    48	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    49	\]
    50	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    51	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    52	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    53	\[
    54	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    55	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    56	\]
    57	Moreover,
    58	\[
    59	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    60	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    61	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq2\delta.
    62	\]
    63	Equivalently, the mean squared distance between the associated binary
    64	projective measurements is at most $\delta$.  The normalization identity and
    65	a counterexample to the stronger operator bound are given in
    66	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}.
    67	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    68	observable is invertible.
    69	
    70	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    71	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    72	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    73	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    74	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    75	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    76	
    77	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    78	
    79	Lines~711--725 of
    80	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    81	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    82	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    83	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    84	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  Moreover,
    85	the provider's equation~(3) proves the bound $\delta$ for binary-measurement
    86	distance; under the operator-distance convention displayed above this is the
    87	bound $2\delta$.  Identifying it with the same bound $\delta$ loses a factor of
    88	two.  The quotation also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the
    89	provider theorem and would unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's
    90	actual defect.  The assertion at the identity follows from exact linearity as
    91	above.
    92	
    93	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    94	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    95	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    96	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    97	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    98	
    99	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
   100	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
   101	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
   102	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
   103	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
   104	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
   105	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
   106	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
   107	
   108	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   109	
   110	Theorem~\path{thm:linearity} and
   111	Remark~\path{rem:linearity-import} in
   112	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex} record respectively the
   113	averaged provider theorem and the common-ancilla obligation for its fiberwise
   114	use.
   115	
   116	The declaration \path{exists_exactly_linear_observables} in
   117	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean} assumes a nonnegative defect, a
   118	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, binary observables, and the averaged
   119	three-observable correlation.  It returns one finite ancillary space and
   120	normalized ancillary vector for that family, exactly linear binary observables
   121	on the extension, and only the averaged squared operator-distance bound.  It
   122	neither assumes $\delta\leq1$ nor asserts pointwise closeness, and it carries
   123	the corrected bound $2\delta$ rather than the printed $\delta$.  It therefore
   124	matches the corrected blueprint theorem, and its proof is complete; so is that
   125	of its measurement-distance companion
   126	\path{exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq}, which states

    47	\section{Key theorem forms}
    48	
    49	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    50	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is
    51	introduced in the next section.
    52	
    53	\begin{enumerate}
    54	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    56	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    57	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    58	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    59	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    61	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    62	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    63	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    64	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    65	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    66	\end{enumerate}
    67	
    68	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    69	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    70	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    71	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    72	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    73	third form.
    74	
    75	\section{The source assertion}
    76	
    77	A two-player one-round game
    78	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    79	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    80	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    81	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    82	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    83	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    84	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    85	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    86	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    87	and the value of the game is the supremum
    88	\begin{equation*}
    89	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    90	\end{equation*}
    91	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    92	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    93	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    94	same measurements.
    95	
    96	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    97	\footnote{The statement is at
    98	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    99	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement kept in this form
   100	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
   101	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
   102	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   103	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   104	\begin{equation*}
   105	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   106	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   107	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   108	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   109	\end{equation*}
   110	
   111	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   112	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   113	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   114	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   115	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   116	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   117	\begin{equation*}
   118	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   119	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   120	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   121	\end{equation*}
   122	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   123	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   124	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   125	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   126	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   127	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   128	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   129	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   130	
   131	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   132	
   133	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   134	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   135	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   136	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   137	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   138	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   139	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   140	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   141	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   142	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   143	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   144	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   145	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   146	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   147	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   148	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   149	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   150	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   151	form.
   152	
   153	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   154	
   155	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   156	
   157	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   158	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   159	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   160	generality that it is projective.%
   161	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   162	lines~317--321.}
   163	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   164	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   165	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   166	
   167	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   168	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   169	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   170	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   171	lines~2322--2332.}
   172	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   173	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   174	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   175	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   176	not used.
   177	
   178	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   179	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   180	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   181	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint records both forms as part of the
   182	games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on either; the two source
   183	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   184	development.
   185	Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here --- requires
   186	the attainment form.
   187	
   188	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   189	
   190	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape,
   191	as the proof-gap protocol requires when the printed statement is not known to
   192	be false and only its proof is blocked.  Its proof records the
   193	value-preserving construction and the approximate form that the construction
   194	yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment step as unproved, citing
   195	this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the obstruction.  The
   196	value-preserving given-strategy form is stated beside it as a separate
   197	formalization-support node, \path{lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy}, which
   198	is not advertised as the source lemma.
   199	
   200	The two Lean declarations follow the same separation.  The source-shaped
   201	\leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is linked to
   202	\path{lem:symmetric-strat}; its proof is the tracked attainment obligation and
   203	remains open.  The given-strategy
   204	\leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy\_of\_strategy}, linked to the
   205	support node, has the same hypothesis, exact value equality, and projective
   206	symmetric conclusion as that node, and its proof is complete.
   207	
   208	\section{Conclusion}
   209	
   210	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   211	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   212	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   213	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built
   214	on the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   215	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   216	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   217	suffices.  Stage~4 has carried out the recommendation of this note: the
   218	given-strategy symmetrization lemma is formalized and proved as the workhorse
   219	statement, while the source-labelled lemma keeps its source shape with the
   220	attainment step an explicit, tracked proof obligation.  If a later
   221	investigation settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the
   222	statement should then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented

    20	
    21	\section{At a glance}
    22	
    23	\begin{itemize}
    24	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  A product expansion computes the
    25	  probability exactly and exposes two false claims in the printed proof.
    26	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal correction consists of one
    27	  finite-field counting theorem and elementary real inequalities, roughly
    28	  100--180 lines.
    29	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} About 40\% finite counting and real
    30	  inequalities, and 60\% project-local finite-field coordinates and sampling.
    31	  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs.} Uniform finite distributions, field-trace
    32	  fibers, Bernoulli's inequality, and the fixed self-dual basis.  The formal
    33	  proof is tracked in \ghissue{110}.
    34	\end{itemize}
    35	
    36	\section{Key theorem forms}
    37	
    38	Let $q=2^k$, let $u_X,u_Z$ be uniform in $\F_q^m$, and let $r_X,r_Z$ be
    39	uniform in $\F_q$.  Put
    40	\[
    41	  \gamma=\tr\big((r_X\ind_m(u_X))\cdot(r_Z\ind_m(u_Z))\big).
    42	\]
    43	Then
    44	\[
    45	  \Pr[\gamma\ne0]=\frac12(1-q^{-1})^{m+1},
    46	  \qquad
    47	  \Pr[\gamma=0]\geq\frac12.
    48	\]
    49	In particular, $m\leq q$ gives the uniform lower bound
    50	$\Pr[\gamma\ne0]\geq2^{-4}$.  If $m,d\geq1$, the two lower bounds printed in
    51	the source also hold:
    52	\[
    53	  \Pr[\gamma\ne0]
    54	  \geq \frac12(1-q^{-m})(1-q^{-1})(1-md/q)
    55	  \geq \frac12(1-3md/q),
    56	\]
    57	and $\Pr[\gamma=0]\geq\frac12(1-3md/q)$.
    58	
    59	\section{The source assertion and discrepancy}
    60	
    61	Fact \path{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} of the Pauli analysis
    62	\cite[lines~64--93]{Ji2020MIPStar} states the last two bounds without the
    63	positivity assumptions on $m$ and $d$.  Its proof starts by
    64	asserting that $\ind_m(u_X)=0$ if and only if $u_X=0$, and that $u_X=0$ forces
    65	$\gamma=0$.%
    66	\footnote{See
    67	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
    68	lines~64--93.}
    69	Both assertions are false.  The coordinates of $\ind_m(u)$ sum to one, so the
    70	indicator vector never vanishes.  For $(q,m,d)=(2,1,0)$ and
    71	$(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)=(0,0,1,1)$, the phase is nonzero.  In the same parameter
    72	case the exact anticommuting probability is $1/8$, below the printed lower
    73	bound $1/2$.  Thus the missing hypothesis $d\geq1$ is mathematically necessary
    74	for that displayed bound.
    75	
    76	\section{The corrected calculation}
    77	
    78	In characteristic two, expansion over the Boolean cube gives
    79	\[
    80	  \ind_m(u_X)\cdot\ind_m(u_Z)
    81	  =\prod_{i=1}^m(1+u_{X,i}+u_{Z,i}).
    82	\]
    83	For fixed $u_X$, the factors are independent and uniform as $u_Z$ varies, so
    84	they are all nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$.  Independently,
    85	$r_X\ne0$ with probability $1-q^{-1}$.  Conditioned on these events, the
    86	argument of the trace is uniform as $r_Z$ varies, and a nonzero linear trace
    87	to $\F_2$ takes the value one with probability $1/2$.  This proves the exact
    88	formula.  Bernoulli's inequality gives the stated source bounds when
    89	$m,d\geq1$; the admissible Pauli-test parameters satisfy these conditions.
    90	
    91	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    92	
    93	The blueprint states the exact probability, restores $m,d\geq1$ on the
    94	source bounds, and uses the unconditional constant lower bound when
    95	conditioning the winning implications.  Its proof and correction remark cite
    96	this note.  The corresponding formal declarations have the same corrected
    97	statements, but their proofs remain open in the current tree.%
    98	\footnote{The declarations are \leanid{anticommProb\_eq},
    99	\leanid{commProb\_ge\_half}, \leanid{anticommProb\_ge\_of\_m\_le\_q}, and
   100	\leanid{anticommProb\_ge\_of\_one\_le\_md} in
   101	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/Anticommuting.lean}.}
   102	
   103	\section{Conclusion}
   104	
   105	The source proof is incorrect, and its displayed bound fails when $d=0$.
   106	The exact probability is $\frac12(1-q^{-1})^{m+1}$.  It yields universal
   107	conditioning probabilities for all admissible parameters and recovers the
   108	printed lower bounds after making the implicit positivity assumptions explicit.

    21	\section{At a glance}
    22	
    23	\begin{itemize}
    24	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The printed upper index is incompatible
    25	  with both the binary coordinate array and the target tensor power.
    26	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One statement correction and no additional
    27	  proof beyond the existing coordinatewise isomorphism.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The correction is entirely
    29	  project-local notation; the proof uses finite tensor products and the fixed
    30	  self-dual basis.
    31	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} A field of size $q=2^k$ has $k$
    32	  binary coordinates, and one $q$-dimensional qudit is identified with $k$
    33	  qubits.  This audit is tracked in \ghissue{173}.
    34	\end{itemize}
    35	
    36	\section{Key theorem forms}
    37	
    38	For $q=2^k$ and $u\in\F_q^L$, write
    39	$u_i=\sum_{j=1}^k u_{ij}e_j$ in the fixed self-dual basis.  The intended
    40	conjugation identity is
    41	\[
    42	  \tau_u^W
    43	  =\phi^\dagger
    44	    \left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^L\bigotimes_{j=1}^k
    45	      \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}\right)\phi,
    46	\]
    47	where $\phi:(\C^q)^{\ot L}\to(\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$.  The inner tensor index must
    48	range from $1$ through $k$, not from $1$ through $q$.
    49	
    50	\section{The source assertion and discrepancy}
    51	
    52	Lemma \path{lem:pauli-binary} of \cite[Section~4.6]{Ji2020MIPStar} first gives
    53	the correct tensor product with $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and defines each
    54	$u_{ij}$ using the $k$ basis elements $e_1,\ldots,e_k$.  Its final sentence,
    55	however, describes the $(i,j)$-th qubit factor with
    56	$j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$.%
    57	\footnote{See \path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex},
    58	lines~1172--1198.}
    59	For $k>1$ this asks for coordinates $u_{ij}$ that were not defined and for
    60	$Lq$ factors in a target containing only $Lk$ qubits.  The proof immediately
    61	returns to the $k$ binary coordinates.  The occurrence of $q$ is therefore a
    62	typographical error in the mathematical statement.
    63	
    64	\section{The correction}
    65	
    66	Replace the final range by $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$.  Then the factor numbered
    67	$s=(i-1)k+j$ lies between $1$ and $Lk$, and every binary coordinate of every
    68	qudit appears exactly once.  This agrees with the displayed tensor product and
    69	with the proof by tensoring the one-qudit coordinate isomorphism.
    70	
    71	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    72	
    73	The blueprint statement of \path{lem:pauli-binary} uses the corrected range
    74	$1\leq j\leq k$, and its proof and source-correction remark cite this note.
    75	The formal theorem indexes the inner factors by the binary-basis dimension and
    76	therefore matches the corrected statement.  Its proof is complete in the
    77	current tree.%
    78	\footnote{The linked declaration is \leanid{exists\_qubitIsometry} in
    79	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean}.}
    80	
    81	\section{Conclusion}
    82	
    83	The upper bound $q$ in the source's final index range is a typographical error.
    84	The correct bound is $k=\log_2 q$, as required by the binary coordinate map,
    85	the target dimension, and the proof.

    39	\section{Key theorem forms}
    40	
    41	For an admissible tuple $(q,m,d)$ and a strategy that wins the Pauli basis test
    42	with probability at least $1-\eps$, each subtest has conditional failure
    43	$O(\eps)$.  In particular, the Magic Square average is conditioned on
    44	\[
    45	  \gamma(\omega)
    46	  =\tr\big((r_X\ind_m(u_X))\cdot(r_Z\ind_m(u_Z))\big)\ne0,
    47	\]
    48	and the low-degree line-evaluation family is completed on zero-direction lines
    49	by an additional outcome.  The observable consequence is
    50	\[
    51	  X^{r_X}(u_X)Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)
    52	  \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
    53	  (-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)X^{r_X}(u_X)
    54	\]
    55	on average over all tuples.  These statements hold for every admissible
    56	parameter tuple; no assumption $6md\leq q$ is needed.

    58	\section{The source assertions and discrepancies}
    59	
    60	The source states the measurement implications at lines~197--265 and the
    61	observable implications at lines~267--362 of the Pauli analysis
    62	\cite[lines~197--362]{Ji2020MIPStar}.%
    63	\footnote{See
    64	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.}
    65	Four corrections are required.
    66	
    67	First, the displayed conditioning event for the Magic Square average omits
    68	$\ind_m$ and writes the scalar expression
    69	$\tr((r_Xu_X)\cdot(r_Zu_Z))$, even though $u_X,u_Z\in\F_q^m$ and the phase
    70	used by the game is defined through vectors in $\F_q^{2^m}$.

    72	Second, the proof assumes $6md\leq q$ and disposes of the complementary range
    73	by appealing to the final Pauli soundness theorem, whose proof uses the lemma
    74	under discussion.  That appeal cannot prove the lemma as an unrestricted
    75	standalone result.  The corrected exact probability calculation gives
    76	universal lower bounds for both conditioning events whenever the parameters
    77	are admissible, and removes this circular reduction.%

    79	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_anticommuting-probability.tex}.}

    82	indexed by $\F_q$.  A zero-direction line admits nonconstant polynomial
    83	representatives with no well-defined value on its singleton image, so these
    84	classes form only a sub-measurement.  Adding an outcome $\bot$ for the missing
    85	mass makes the consistency relation well typed; the point family is completed

    91	\path{len:qld-win-implications-obs} is likewise a typographical error for
    92	\path{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}.

    97	sampling weight.  For admissible parameters, $1\leq m\leq q$, and the exact

    33	\section{Key theorem forms}
    34	Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb F_p$, let
    35	$\chi(x)=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_p}(x)/p)$, and let
    36	$a,a',b\in K^n$.  The relevant identities are
    37	\[
    38	 \tau^W(a)\tau^W(a')=\tau^W(a+a'),\qquad
    39	 \tau^W(a)^p=I,
    40	\]
    41	and
    42	\[
    43	 \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)=\chi(-a\mathbin{\cdot}b)
    44	 \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    45	\]
    46	The explicit shift and phase matrices are unitary. The second identity implies
    47	that every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $\tau^W(a)$ satisfies $\lambda^p=1$. If
    48	$V\leq K^n$ and $v\notin V^\perp$, Fourier cancellation takes the form
    49	\[
    50	 \mathbb E_{u\in V}\chi(u\mathbin{\cdot}v)=0.
    51	\]
    52	Writing $P_b^W$ for the rank-one projector onto the $b$-labelled vector in the
    53	$W$ eigenbasis, the forward expansion and its Fourier inverse are
    54	\[
    55	 \tau^W(a)=\sum_{b\in K^n}\chi(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)P_b^W,
    56	 \qquad
    57	 P_b^W=\mathbb E_{a\in K^n}\chi(-a\mathbin{\cdot}b)\tau^W(a).
    58	\]
    59	
    60	\section{Source and formal scope}
    61	The source defines the shift and phase matrices and states their product,
    62	$p$-th-power, unitarity, spectral, and twisted-commutation properties in
    63	\cite[lines 1056--1095]{Ji2020MIPStar}. It uses the same character for Fourier
    64	cancellation over a subspace at lines 1124--1132.  The single-qudit forward and
    65	inverse expansions occur at lines 1118--1139, and their multi-qudit forms occur
    66	at lines 1151--1161.  These assertions use the characteristic-$p$ character;
    67	they are not intrinsically binary.
    68	
    69	The formal definitions \path{primeTauShift}, \path{primeTauPhase}, and
    70	\path{primeTauObservable} use the canonical character \path{ffChar} in
    71	characteristic $p$.  Their theorem statements cover the product, power,
    72	unitarity, spectral, commutation, and cancellation identities for arbitrary
    73	$p$.  The source-general forward expansion and inversion do not yet have
    74	corresponding Lean declarations.  The declarations whose names begin with
    75	\path{tauObservable} or use \path{phaseSign} instead specialize to $p=2$, where
    76	$\chi(x)=(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(x)}$.  This specialization is appropriate only
    77	for the subsequent test, whose admissible sizes satisfy $q=2^k$; it is not
    78	substituted for the general statements.
    79	
    80	In characteristic two, $-x=x$, so the negative phase in the inverse expansion
    81	is the same \path{phaseSign} used in the forward expansion.  Thus
    82	\leanid{tauObservable\_eq\_sum\_pauliProj} and
    83	\leanid{pauliProj\_eq\_avg\_tauObservable} prove precisely the two displayed
    84	formulas for finite fields carrying an algebra over $\mathbb F_2$.  Their proof
    85	uses additive-character orthogonality after transporting the coordinate type
    86	along an equivalence with a finite ordinal; the restriction enters only through
    87	the identification of the canonical character with \path{phaseSign}.
    88	
    89	The proofs can be obtained directly from the displayed matrices.  A shift is a
    90	permutation matrix, a phase matrix has diagonal entries of modulus one, and a
    91	tensor product of such matrices is unitary.  Iterating the product identity
    92	gives $\tau^W(a)^p=I$.  Applying this equality to a nonzero eigenvector gives
    93	$(\lambda^p-1)v=0$, hence $\lambda^p=1$.  Finally, when
    94	$v\notin V^\perp$, the map $u\mapsto\chi(u\cdot v)$ is a nontrivial character
    95	of the finite additive group $V$, so its average vanishes.

    61	\section{Key theorem forms}
    62	
    63	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    64	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    65	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    66	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    67	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    68	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    69	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    70	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    71	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    72	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    73	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    74	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    75	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    76	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    77	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    78	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    79	register-swapped counterpart.%
    80	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    81	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    82	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    83	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    84	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    85	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    86	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    87	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    88	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    89	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    90	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    91	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}

    93	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.

   116	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   117	
   118	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   119	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   120	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   121	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   122	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   123	\begin{equation}
   124	  \Lambda \,=\,
   125	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   126	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   127	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   128	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   129	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   130	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,
   131	  \tag{\path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}}
   132	\end{equation}
   133	in which the point $(x,z,\alpha,\beta)$ is uniform on $\ell$ and the sum
   134	ranges over pairs of line polynomials.  The proof then bounds $\Lambda$
   135	twice, by different routes and with different results, and the printed
   136	record is internally inconsistent: the display introducing $\Lambda$
   137	asserts the first-route bound, while the closing lines assert the
   138	second-route bound as the operative one; the lemma statement claims a
   139	third form matching neither.
   140	
   141	\paragraph{The first route.}
   142	Three claims are chained.  The combined point measurement
   143	$\hat Q^{x,z}$ is replaced by the ordered product of the two point
   144	measurements at cost $\delta_Q^{1/2}$; the $X$-point factor is removed at
   145	cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$; and the remaining $Z$-point
   146	correlation is shown to be within
   147	$\sqrt{m}\,(\delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} + \eps^{1/4})$ of one.  The
   148	factors of $m$ enter through the mixture structure of the sub-line
   149	distribution: each restricted line distribution carries mixture weight
   150	$1/(2m)$ in the line-point distribution, so an average bounded by
   151	$\delta$ over the full distribution is bounded only by $2m\delta$ over a
   152	restricted component and by $4m^2\delta$ over a product of two
   153	components, and the Cauchy--Schwarz steps halve the exponents.  Chaining
   154	the claims gives
   155	\begin{equation*}
   156	  \Lambda \,=\, O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   157	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)
   158	  \,=\, m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)\,.
   159	\end{equation*}
   160	One intermediate assertion needs a harmless correction: the final line
   161	of the proof of the second claim asserts the bound
   162	$O(m^2 \delta_{\mathrm{Line}})$ for a consistency term that is close to
   163	one, rather than for its deficit.  Read as a bound on the deficit ---
   164	which is what the surrounding Cauchy--Schwarz argument requires and what
   165	the invoked line--point consistency provides after the mixture
   166	inflation --- the claim and its use are correct, with the square root of
   167	the deficit giving the stated cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$.
   168	
   169	\paragraph{The second route.}
   170	After the chain, the source restarts: it asserts that, by Property~2 of
   171	its sub-line lemma, $\Lambda$ is a mixture, over types
   172	$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and
   173	indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$, of terms
   174	\begin{equation*}
   175	  \E_{(\ell_X, x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
   176	  \E_{(\ell_Z, z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
   177	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   178	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   179	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   180	  \ket{\hat\psi}
   181	\end{equation*}
   182	over two \emph{independently} sampled restricted line-point pairs,
   183	bounds each term by $O(m^2\delta_P)$ using the restricted-distribution
   184	consequence of the two-basis line lemma, and concludes
   185	$\Lambda = O(m^2\delta_P)$.  The invoked decomposition concerns the
   186	\emph{joint} law of the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$, where $x$ and
   187	$z$ are the two blocks of the single point sampled on $\ell$.  Property~2
   188	of the sub-line lemma does not assert this joint law: it asserts the
   189	component-wise product law of the pair of \emph{lines}
   190	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, and the conditional uniformity of each point on its
   191	line separately --- equivalently, the laws of the two pairs
   192	$((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z'))$ and $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, z))$ in which
   193	the \emph{other} point is resampled independently.  These marginal
   194	statements are exactly what the first route's claims consume, each
   195	involving one point at a time; the joint decomposition used by the
   196	second route is a strictly stronger property and is not established by
   197	the lemma it is attributed to.
   198	
   199	\section{Why neither route yields the stated form}
   200	
   201	The stated error form is $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, a function of the two
   202	quantities $m^2\eps$ and $md/q$ that vanishes as both vanish.  The
   203	first-route bound is not dominated by any such function: along the
   204	scaling $\eps = m^{-4}$ with $q/(md) \to \infty$, both $m^2\eps = m^{-2}$
   205	and $md/q$ tend to $0$, while the term $m\,\eps^{1/4} = 1$ does not.
   206	Hence the established derivation supports no bound of the claimed form.
   207	The second-route bound, even granting the missing decomposition, carries
   208	the separate prefactor $m^2$: writing $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$
   209	with some fixed positive exponents, the contribution
   210	$m^2 (md/q)^{c}$ is not dominated by any vanishing function of $m^2\eps$
   211	and $md/q$, as the scaling $\eps = 0$, $md/q = m^{-2/c}$ shows, and the
   212	$\eps$-contribution fails similarly for sublinear exponents.  Neither
   213	observation asserts that the \emph{conclusion} of the lemma is false for
   214	some error function of the claimed form; the defect is that the printed
   215	proof does not deliver it.
   216	
   217	For orientation, the algebraic identity
   218	$m\,\eps^{1/2} = (m^2\eps)^{1/2}$ shows what a derivation of the claimed
   219	$\eps$-dependence would need: a chain that loses only square roots in the
   220	$\eps$-type quantities \emph{after} the restricted-distribution
   221	inflation would produce terms of the shape $(m^2\eps)^{1/2}$.  The
   222	printed chain loses fourth roots, through two nested Cauchy--Schwarz
   223	steps applied to already square-rooted quantities, and its
   224	$md/q$-dependence enters as $m\,\delta_P^{1/4}$, which the claimed form
   225	cannot absorb.
   226	
   227	\section{Correction and alternative repairs}
   228	
   229	The first direction below is the one the blueprint adopts; the remaining
   230	directions are alternatives, none of which is claimed as established.
   231	
   232	\paragraph{Corrected error form (adopted in the proof).}
   233	The operative error form is
   234	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ --- concretely,
   235	the first-route bound.  Following the proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled
   236	statement keeps its printed form and the correction is carried by the proof,
   237	by the chapter remark, and by a separate formalization-support node, rather
   238	than being substituted silently into the source statement.  The only consumer
   239	is the polynomial-pair lemma, whose imported error
   240	$a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ absorbs
   241	$m^{O(1)}$ prefactors by enlarging $a$ and shrinking $b$.  The blueprint proof
   242	records this absorption and the corrected deficit reading of the second claim.
   243	Two obligations remain: carry out that absorption with explicit constants when
   244	the lemma is formalized, and prove the three chained estimates.
   245	
   246	\paragraph{Repairing the second route.}
   247	Strengthen Property~2 of the sub-line lemma to the joint product law: in
   248	each mixture component, the pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ are
   249	independent with the stated restricted-distribution laws.  The sampling
   250	procedure makes this plausible, since in each component the two pairs
   251	are built from disjoint collections of the independent ingredients (the
   252	two blocks of the uniform point, the direction blocks, and the fresh
   253	auxiliary choices).  Open obligations: (i)~state and prove the
   254	strengthened property for every component, including lines whose
   255	direction blocks vanish and degenerate to singletons; (ii)~re-derive the
   256	mixture decomposition of $\Lambda$ from the strengthened property;
   257	(iii)~note that even then the route delivers only
   258	$O(m^2\delta_P) = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, so this direction removes
   259	the unsupported step of the printed proof but still requires the
   260	error-form decision of the previous direction, with $m^2$ in place of
   261	$m$.
   262	
   263	\paragraph{Establishing the claimed form.}
   264	Re-derive the chain so that every factor of $m$ enters jointly with
   265	$\eps$ as $m^2\eps$, in the sense of the orientation identity above.
   266	Open obligations: (i)~find a chaining that avoids one of the two nested
   267	square-root losses, or prove restricted-distribution versions of the
   268	underlying consistency lemmas directly at their inflated errors;
   269	(ii)~handle the $md/q$-dependence, since a residual term
   270	$m (md/q)^{c}$ is incompatible with the claimed form for the current
   271	exponents.  No derivation along these lines is known here, and the
   272	direction may be infeasible; in that case the corrected error form of
   273	the first direction stands.
   274	
   275	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   276	
   277	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the combined-lines lemma in
   278	its source shape, error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$ included, and marks in
   279	the proof that this form remains unproved: the proof derives the first route
   280	only, records the established bound $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, and uses
   281	that bound in the sequel.  The
   282	three claims are stated as separate lemmas with the corrected deficit
   283	assertion for the second; the sub-line lemma states Property~2 at the
   284	level of the two marginal laws and expressly disclaims the joint
   285	conditional law of the two points, so the blueprint statement does not
   286	license the second route; and the polynomial-pair lemma's proof absorbs
   287	the $m$ prefactor into the constants of the imported soundness error.  A
   288	chapter remark summarizes the discrepancy and cites this note.%
   289	\footnote{The blueprint statements are \path{lem:qld-4-13},
   290	\path{lem:qld-sublines}, \path{lem:claim-17-1}--\path{lem:claim-17-3},
   291	\path{lem:qld-4-7}, and the remark
   292	\path{rem:qld-4-13-source-defects}, all in
   293	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   294	
   295	The source-labelled lemma links the carrier
   296	\path{ExtendedLinesWitness} and the source-shaped declaration
   297	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness}, which retains the printed error form
   298	$\poly(m^2\eps,md/q)$ and whose proof is the tracked obligation.  The
   299	established error form is linked from the separate formalization-support node
   300	\path{lem:qld-4-13-established}, whose declaration
   301	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} has the explicit form
   302	$C m\,\poly(\eps,md/q)$ for a universal $C>0$; this agrees with the blueprint
   303	convention that constants are absorbed into $\poly$.  Its proof is open as
   304	well, so neither node carries a proof-completion mark.
   305	
   306	\section{Conclusion}
   307	
   308	There is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma, together with an
   309	intermediate inconsistency: the printed proof asserts two different
   310	bounds for the same consistency defect, the first-route bound
   311	$O(m(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} +
   312	\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}))$ and the second-route bound
   313	$O(m^2\delta_P)$, the second resting on a joint-law decomposition that
   314	the sub-line lemma as stated does not supply; and the error form claimed
   315	in the lemma statement, $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, follows from neither.
   316	The first route is sound after a harmless deficit correction in its
   317	second claim and establishes $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$.  The
   318	discrepancy is harmless downstream, since the sole consumer absorbs
   319	polynomial-in-$m$ prefactors into its constants.  The blueprint therefore
   320	retains the printed statement with the missing step explicitly tracked, uses
   321	the corrected first-route form in the proof and in the sequel, and cites this
   322	note; strengthening the sub-line lemma to license the second route is
   323	optional, and no route to the printed form is currently known.  We do not
   324	assert that the printed form is false.

    16	\date{2026-09-04}
    17	
    18	\begin{document}
    19	\maketitle
    20	
    21	\section{At a glance}
    22	
    23	\begin{itemize}
    24	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low to medium.  The subtest implications are
    25	  direct after conditioning, but the printed proof uses an invalid parameter
    26	  reduction and two displayed formulas contain wrong indices.
    27	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal work is the family of exact and
    28	  approximate winning implications, roughly 300--500 lines after the sampling
    29	  probability results are available.
    30	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} About 20\% finite-probability
    31	  bookkeeping and 80\% project-local game predicates, post-processing, and
    32	  state-dependent distance transfer.
    33	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Constant lower bounds for the
    34	  commuting and anticommuting events, data processing, and the one-way Magic
    35	  Square rigidity theorem.  The proof packets are \ghissue{112} and
    36	  \ghissue{113}.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	
    39	\section{Key theorem forms}
    40	
    41	For an admissible tuple $(q,m,d)$ and a strategy that wins the Pauli basis test
    42	with probability at least $1-\eps$, each subtest has conditional failure
    43	$O(\eps)$.  In particular, the Magic Square average is conditioned on
    44	\[
    45	  \gamma(\omega)
    46	  =\tr\big((r_X\ind_m(u_X))\cdot(r_Z\ind_m(u_Z))\big)\ne0,
    47	\]
    48	and the low-degree line-evaluation family is completed on zero-direction lines
    49	by an additional outcome.  The observable consequence is
    50	\[
    51	  X^{r_X}(u_X)Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)
    52	  \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
    53	  (-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)X^{r_X}(u_X)
    54	\]
    55	on average over all tuples.  These statements hold for every admissible
    56	parameter tuple; no assumption $6md\leq q$ is needed.
    57	
    58	\section{The source assertions and discrepancies}
    59	
    60	The source states the measurement implications at lines~197--265 and the
    61	observable implications at lines~267--362 of the Pauli analysis
    62	\cite[lines~197--362]{Ji2020MIPStar}.%
    63	\footnote{See
    64	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.}
    65	Four corrections are required.
    66	
    67	First, the displayed conditioning event for the Magic Square average omits
    68	$\ind_m$ and writes the scalar expression
    69	$\tr((r_Xu_X)\cdot(r_Zu_Z))$, even though $u_X,u_Z\in\F_q^m$ and the phase
    70	used by the game is defined through vectors in $\F_q^{2^m}$.
    71	
    72	Second, the proof assumes $6md\leq q$ and disposes of the complementary range
    73	by appealing to the final Pauli soundness theorem, whose proof uses the lemma
    74	under discussion.  That appeal cannot prove the lemma as an unrestricted
    75	standalone result.  The corrected exact probability calculation gives
    76	universal lower bounds for both conditioning events whenever the parameters
    77	are admissible, and removes this circular reduction.%
    78	\footnote{The probability correction is documented separately in
    79	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_anticommuting-probability.tex}.}
    80	
    81	Third, the source treats evaluation classes of a line measurement as a POVM
    82	indexed by $\F_q$.  A zero-direction line admits nonconstant polynomial
    83	representatives with no well-defined value on its singleton image, so these
    84	classes form only a sub-measurement.  Adding an outcome $\bot$ for the missing
    85	mass makes the consistency relation well typed; the point family is completed
    86	by a zero effect at the same outcome.
    87	
    88	Finally, the observable proof writes
    89	$Z^{r_X}(u_X)X^{r_Z}(u_Z)$ where the intended reversed product is
    90	$Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)X^{r_X}(u_X)$.  The source label prefix
    91	\path{len:qld-win-implications-obs} is likewise a typographical error for
    92	\path{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}.
    93	
    94	\section{The corrected argument}
    95	
    96	Every question type and every relevant subtest has a universal positive
    97	sampling weight.  For admissible parameters, $1\leq m\leq q$, and the exact
    98	calculation of the anticommuting probability gives probability at least
    99	$2^{-4}$ for the anticommuting event and at least $1/2$ for its complement.
   100	Conditioning therefore enlarges rejection probabilities only by a universal
   101	factor.  The measurement implications follow directly from their rejection
   102	events, including the completed zero-direction outcome.  Data processing and
   103	the agreement identities yield the observable relations; the corrected Magic
   104	Square phase and reversed product then give the displayed signed commutation
   105	law.
   106	
   107	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   108	
   109	The blueprint uses the full phase $\gamma$, completes the line-evaluation
   110	families, proves the conditioning step with the universal probability bounds,
   111	and corrects the reversed product and label.  Its proof and correction remark
   112	cite this note.  The linked formal declarations use the same conditional
   113	distributions and completed line outcomes, so their statements agree with the
   114	corrected blueprint.  Their proofs remain open in the current tree.%
   115	\footnote{The relevant declarations are \leanid{win\_cons},
   116	\leanid{win\_low\_degree}, \leanid{win\_pauli\_basis\_cons},
   117	\leanid{win\_comm}, \leanid{win\_comm\_cons},
   118	\leanid{win\_magic\_square}, \leanid{win\_ms\_cons}, and their
   119	\path{\_approx} companions in
   120	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/WinImplications.lean}.}
   121	
   122	\section{Conclusion}
   123	
   124	The winning implications remain valid for all admissible parameters, but the
   125	printed proof does not establish that scope and several formulas need local
   126	correction.  Exact conditioning probabilities, the explicit missing outcome,
   127	and the corrected phase and operator indices give the form used by the Pauli
   128	basis analysis.

    22

    36	\section{Key theorem forms}
    37	
    38	For $q=2^k$ and $u\in\F_q^L$, write
    39	$u_i=\sum_{j=1}^k u_{ij}e_j$ in the fixed self-dual basis.  The intended
    40	conjugation identity is
    41	\[
    42	  \tau_u^W
    43	  =\phi^\dagger
    44	    \left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^L\bigotimes_{j=1}^k
    45	      \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}\right)\phi,
    46	\]
    47	where $\phi:(\C^q)^{\ot L}\to(\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$.  The inner tensor index must
    48	range from $1$ through $k$, not from $1$ through $q$.
    49	
    50	\section{The source assertion and discrepancy}
    51	
    52	Lemma \path{lem:pauli-binary} of \cite[Section~4.6]{Ji2020MIPStar} first gives
    53	the correct tensor product with $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and defines each
    54	$u_{ij}$ using the $k$ basis elements $e_1,\ldots,e_k$.  Its final sentence,
    55	however, describes the $(i,j)$-th qubit factor with
    56	$j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$.%
    57	\footnote{See \path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex},
    58	lines~1172--1198.}
    59	For $k>1$ this asks for coordinates $u_{ij}$ that were not defined and for
    60	$Lq$ factors in a target containing only $Lk$ qubits.  The proof immediately
    61	returns to the $k$ binary coordinates.  The occurrence of $q$ is therefore a
    62	typographical error in the mathematical statement.
    63	
    64	\section{The correction}
    65	
    66	Replace the final range by $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$.  Then the factor numbered
    67	$s=(i-1)k+j$ lies between $1$ and $Lk$, and every binary coordinate of every
    68	qudit appears exactly once.  This agrees with the displayed tensor product and
    69	with the proof by tensoring the one-qudit coordinate isomorphism.
    70	
    71	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    72	
    73	The blueprint statement of \path{lem:pauli-binary} uses the corrected range
    74	$1\leq j\leq k$, and its proof and source-correction remark cite this note.
    75	The formal theorem indexes the inner factors by the binary-basis dimension and
    76	therefore matches the corrected statement.  Its proof is complete in the
    77	current tree.%
    78	\footnote{The linked declaration is \leanid{exists\_qubitIsometry} in
    79	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean}.}
    80	
    81	\section{Conclusion}
    82	
    83	The upper bound $q$ in the source's final index range is a typographical error.
    84	The correct bound is $k=\log_2 q$, as required by the binary coordinate map,
    85	the target dimension, and the proof.

   211			\item \label{enu:qld-comm-cons} (\textbf{Commutation consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_{a}$, where the answer summation is over $a\in \F_2$.

Then

   216	                          u_\xpt) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot u_\zpt)) \neq 0} \Lambda_\omega = 1 - O(\eps)\;.

   260	  Square check in \cref{fig:decider_pauli} is executed with constant probability
   261	  over the choice of a pair of questions.

   708		basis test (Definition~\ref{def:pauli-question-distribution}), which has
   709		constant size, so each subtest of the win predicate
   710		(Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}) is executed with probability
   711		bounded below by a universal constant.

   713		and~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} then follow directly from the
   714		corresponding subtests and the assumption that $\mathcal{S}$ succeeds
   715		with probability at least $1-\eps$, where item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} follows
   716		from the consistency subtest of the low individual degree game executed
   717		inside the Pauli basis test. In more detail for item~\ref{enu:qld-ld}:
   718		the disagreement mass of the two completed families is rejection mass
   719		of the line-versus-point clauses
   720		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}, invoked by the low-degree
   721		check of Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}). An outcome pair
   722		$(a,b)$ with $a \neq b$ in $\F_q$ is a line answer evaluating at $u$
   723		to $a$ against the point answer $b$, which the clause rejects; a pair
   724		$(\bot,b)$ is a line answer with no evaluation at $u$, which the
   725		universally quantified clause rejects against every point answer $b$
   726		(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction} and
   727		Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}); and the pairs $(a,\bot)$
   728		contribute no mass, since the class
   729		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot}$ is the zero operator. The subtests underlying
   730		items~\ref{enu:qld-comm} and~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} accept vacuously
   731		unless the sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting, and those underlying
   732		items~\ref{enu:qld-ms} and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} accept vacuously
   733		unless $\omega$ is anticommuting. Since the parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   734		is admissible (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), $m$ divides $q$, so
   735		$1 \leq m \leq q$, and Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} shows that
   736		a uniformly sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting with probability at
   737		least $\frac12$ and anticommuting with probability at least $2^{-4}$.

   739		probability of the corresponding subtest by a factor of at most $2^4$,

   741		and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} follow from the corresponding subtests.

   743		check is executed with constant probability over the choice of a pair
   744		of questions and the anticommuting event has probability at least
   745		$2^{-4}$.  This replacement for the source's circular parameter reduction
   746		is documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_win-implications-corrections}. Finally, that all approximations
   747		also hold with $\approx_\eps$ in place of $\simeq_\eps$ is immediate
   748		from Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.

136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
   144	  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
   145	  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
   146	  line range, or blueprint result it supports.
   147	- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
   148	  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
   149	  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
   150	  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
   151	  Lean proof.
   152	- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
   153	  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
   154	  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
   155	  used.
   156	- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
   157	  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
   158	  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
   159	  proof remains tracked as incomplete.

   112	
   113	\paragraph{Repair.}
   114	A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
   115	partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
   116	the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
   117	orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
   118	should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
   119	corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
   120	of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.
   121	
   122	\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
   123	An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
   124	needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
   125	or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
   126	drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
   127	inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
   128	proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
   129	obligation.
   130	
   131	\section{The main failure mode}
   132	
   133	Suppose the paper proves
   134	\[
   135	  H \Longrightarrow C.
   136	\]
   137	During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
   138	paper theorem should be represented as
   139	\[
   140	  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
   141	  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
   142	\]
   143	where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
   144	public statement is a different theorem:
   145	\[
   146	  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
   147	\]
   148	It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
   149	conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
   150	conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
   151	conclusion.
   152	
   153	This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
   154	hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
   155	from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
   156	the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
   157	paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
   158	named internal proof obligation.
   159	
   160	\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}
   161	
   162	Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
   163	faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
   164	nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
   165	quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
   166	or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
   167	when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
   168	condition used implicitly in the paper.
   169	
   170	The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
   171	domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
   172	mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
   173	leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
   174	hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.
   175	
   176	\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}
   177	
   178	Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
   179	definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
   180	then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
   181	while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
   182	can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
   183	the wrong definition is still upstream.
   184	
   185	When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
   186	protocol.
   187	
   188	\begin{enumerate}
   189	  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
   190	  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
   191	  relating the existing definition to the source object.
   192	  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
   193	  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
   194	  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
   195	  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
   196	  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
   197	\end{enumerate}
   198	
   199	This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
   200	definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.
   201	
   202	\section{Allowed shapes}
   203	
   204	\begin{center}
   205	\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
   206	\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
   207	\hline
   208	Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
   209	Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
   210	proof-obligation hypotheses \\
   211	Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
   212	source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
   213	theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
   214	Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
   215	remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
   216	avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
   217	proof-complete for that theorem \\
   218	Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
   219	Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
   220	Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
   221	source theorem instead of being produced \\
   222	Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
   223	fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
   224	Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
   225	Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
   226	\end{tabular}
   227	\end{center}
   228	
   229	\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}
   230	
   231	When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.
   232	
   233	\begin{enumerate}
   234	  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
   235	  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
   236	  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
   237	  first missing intermediate assertion.
   238	  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
   239	  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
   240	  paper-gap discrepancy.
   241	  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
   242	  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
   243	  hypothesis.
   244	  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
   245	  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
   246	  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
   247	  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
   248	  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
   249	  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
   250	  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
   251	  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
   252	  it.
   253	  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
   254	  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
   255	  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
   256	  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
   257	  notes, not in the source theorem block.
   258	\end{enumerate}
